About

✨ What's new in 1.4

  • New in 1.4.1: Viksit Bharat 2047 gets a light, premium makeover. Ivory pages, white cards and saffron and green accents, with the Ashoka Chakra in navy. Your game, saves and best scores stay the same.
  • A brighter, more refined look. Airy ivory surfaces, elegant new headings, softer shadows, and each game's own colours as gentle highlights.
  • Light by default. The app now stays light even when your phone is in dark mode. Prefer dark? Choose Appearance in Settings: Light, Dark or Auto.
  • A new, brighter app icon and light launch screens.
  • Smoother touches: gentle depth as you scroll, springy buttons and a burst of confetti for a new best. All motion follows your Reduce motion setting.
  • Everything else stays: English, हिन्दी and ਪੰਜਾਬੀ, offline play, your saves and best scores.
Earlier versions

1.3

  • A fresh, vibrant look. A new home screen with one big card per game, bold colours for each game, and a new HRS Games logo and app icon.
  • हिन्दी and ਪੰਜਾਬੀ. Choose English, Hindi or Punjabi in Settings or with the 🌐 chip on the home screen. The app and both new games, Viksit Bharat 2047 and SDG 2030, switch instantly, even mid-game.
  • Fewer words, quicker play. Big Play and Continue buttons, best scores as small chips, and game details and earlier editions tucked behind a tap.
  • Settings in a bottom sheet (swipe down to close), plus a time-of-day greeting.
  • Playful touches: cards respond to your touch, pages glide in, and a burst of confetti celebrates a new best score.

1.2

  • Viksit Bharat 2047 now has three levels, picked on the title screen. 🎒 School (ages 10–14): 5 friendly groups, a bigger budget, gentle shocks, kind choices, and a fact and quiz each term. 🎓 College (ages 15–22): trade-off lines, stakeholder dilemmas, and predict-the-number before each fast-forward. 💼 Expert: tighter budgets, harsher shocks and a coalition of farmers, youth, industry and environment to keep happy.
  • Touch-first: bigger buttons, swipe a choice to pick it, long-press a tile for details, and the main button always sits at the bottom.
  • Each level keeps its own best score (your earlier best counts as College). An unfinished game from the previous edition continues in the new one. The v2 edition is still available, next to the Classic edition.
  • SDG 2030 now has three modes. Who's playing? 🎒 School Kids: 10 turns, 2 cards, clear hints, feelings moments and easy quizzes, and you can't fail. 🎓 College (default): 16 seasons, hidden bills, timed concept quizzes and ethical dilemmas. 💼 Adults: 20 seasons, hard calls, lobbyists, elections, compounding storms and a tipping point, with no hints.
  • Each mode keeps its own best score, shown on the home screen. Continue remembers the mode.
  • Better touch controls: bigger tap targets, swipe a card up to play it, tap to open and close tips, and optional vibration (Settings).

1.1

  • Viksit Bharat 2047, new edition: plan India's road to 2047 in seven terms of Event → Plan → Result. Drop coins on sectors and the national power grid, unlock specialisation hubs, and track GDP, grid adequacy, clean power and approval against real 2026 data.
  • SDG 2030: Heal the World, new edition: one screen and one choice per season. Watch a tiny planet heal or decay as you fill all 17 goals. Quick wins pay now, but their storms land later.
  • Both new editions autosave, show Continue and your best score on the home screen, and follow your sound, motion and text-size settings.
  • Classic editions (The Planner's Desk and Race to the Goals) are still here, with your old saves and best scores. Use the small link on each card.

The creator

Harpreet Raj Singh™ designs games that turn real-world challenges (national development, clean energy, climate and the Global Goals) into decisions you can feel.

Mission

The Harpreet Raj Singh App of productive edutainment games for progressive youth and adults of the 21st Century, to steer this Century in a positive direction.

Every game is built on three principles: grounded (real baselines and official targets, clearly separated from invented mechanics), fair (every choice has trade-offs), and playful (humour and surprise, never a lecture).

Disclaimers

  • These games are educational simulations, not forecasts. Real-world baselines are cited in-game; future dynamics and scores are simplified game mechanics.
  • Viksit Bharat 2047 is an independent work. It is not affiliated with, sponsored or endorsed by the Government of India, NITI Aayog or any ministry or agency. Programme names and targets are referenced for education and commentary.
  • SDG 2030 is an independent work. It is not affiliated with, sponsored or endorsed by the United Nations. Sustainable Development Goal names and colours are used for educational purposes; no UN emblem is used. “Veridia” and its rival nations are fictional.
  • Harpreet Raj Singh™ and the game titles are the creator's marks.
